newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Five hundred Sri Lankans get Gulf War compensation.
newsitem.headline: Five hundred Sri Lankans get Gulf War compensation.

text.p: Five hundred Sri Lankans, out of a total of 6,385 eligible for compensation for losses incurred during the Gulf War, have so far received money from a U.N. reparations body, a government official said on Thursday.

A first batch of 500 people received their money earlier this week and the others would get it within the next few weeks, Nissanka Wijeratne, chairman of the Bureau of Foreign Employment, told Reuters.
"We have got money to be distributed amongst 6,385 people. Each of them will receive $2,500," Wijeratne said.

The U.N. Compensation Commission last March paid $144 million to 63 governments for distribution to 57,636 people who proved they were forced to leave Kuwait or Iraq or who lost up to $100,000 during the 1990 invasion of Kuwait by Iraq.

A large number of individuals, corporations and governments have filed claims valued at more than $220 billion against Baghdad for losses directly due to Iraq's invasion and its seven-month occupation of Kuwait.

The U.N. commisson, funded largely by donations and seized Iraqi assets, previously paid $13.4 million in compensation to 3,966 people who had proved the death of a close relative or serious injury to themselves.
They included 40 Sri Lankans who received a total of $130,000, Wijeratne said.
Nearly 600,000 Sri Lankans work in the Middle East, 65 percent are housemaids. Their remittances have been the top foreign exchange earner for Sri Lanka for the past five years.
